subject: Nearest neighbour distances and kernel estimation

messages.author: 04c79a1892117ce4
messages.subject: Nearest neighbour distances and kernel estimation
parts:
Dear list,

I'd like to know if it's possible to use nearest neighbour distances
in combination with ggplot2? In spatstat, one is able to create so-
called Stienen diagrams (http://skitch.com/mbarbosa/b8q62/stienen-
diagram) in which the radius of the circle depicts the nearest
neighbour distance for that point. Is it possible to create such plots
or even additional plots using nearest neighbour distances?

Kind regards,

Michel

surface of the values of the ratings of my restaurants. I'd like to
generate a plot such as http://skitch.com/mbarbosa/b8q9q/smoothing .

Is this possible with ggplot2 as well?

Kind regards,

Michel

messages.author: 69658a5d047f38b4
messages.subject: Re: Nearest neighbour distances and kernel estimation
parts: > Is this possible with ggplot2 as well?

you need to do the interpolation separately and then feed the data to
geom_tile.

I might be wrong, and Hadley will correct me, but ggplot is a
*plotting* package. This means, for me at least, that most computation
is done beforehand and that ggplot comes into play once you have a
data.frame filled with the data you want to represent. Even though
some statistical functions, such as smoothing, contouring,
manipulating scales etc. are directly available, ggplot is not a do-it-
all package in which you would feed the raw data and which would
output the graphics. So basically, I would recommend to use spastat
(or other interpolation packages: kriging, akima etc.) to compute
whatever you need, put that in a data.frame, and then start thinking
about ggplot.

From that point on, the manual and the website should allow you to
find the appropriate function easily (geom_tile is quite obvious in
the documentation).

JiHO
